title: Climb the Wild Great Wall? Up to a ¥30,000 Fine | China Travel Expert
description:
Thinking of climbing the Great Wall's "wild," unrestored sections? Beijing can fine you up to ¥30,000 — roughly $4,400 — for trespassing on the parts that aren't officially open.

Those closed sections are unrestored and unguarded: the stone is steep, broken and easy to slip on, and people really do get lost or fall. Beijing keeps scores of guards on the wall and even watches social media for planned "wild wall" trips. The restored, ticketed sections are just as spectacular — Mutianyu, Jinshanling and Badaling are all open and safe.

🧭 Expert Tip: want a quieter wall without breaking the rules? Jinshanling is officially open, only partly restored, and far less crowded than Badaling.

别爬没开放的"野长城"：北京最高可罚 3 万元，碎石陡坡容易摔伤，去慕田峪、金山岭这些正规段又安全又震撼。
